characterized_levers.name: Participant Recruitment Channels
characterized_levers.consequences: Expanding recruitment channels increases participant flow, potentially accelerating enrollment and event capture. However, broader recruitment may introduce heterogeneity in the participant pool, requiring more stringent screening and potentially affecting the generalizability of findings. Overly broad recruitment can also strain resources allocated for screening and onboarding.
options: Actively recruit through national patient advocacy groups and online forums dedicated to sleep disorders, emphasizing the potential for personalized feedback and contributing to scientific advancement.

Establish a collaborative referral network with general practitioners and community health centers in the Bonn metropolitan area, offering educational seminars on parasomnia recognition and referral pathways.

Partner with local media outlets to run public service announcements and feature stories about the research unit, raising awareness and encouraging self-referral from individuals experiencing parasomnia symptoms.
characterized_levers.review: Expanding recruitment boosts enrollment speed, but introduces selection biases; the options neglect proactive engagement with underserved populations who may lack access to traditional channels.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Participant recruitment is important for enrollment targets, but the specific channels are secondary to the overall recruitment strategy and inclusion/exclusion criteria.
characterized_levers.description: Purpose: The Participant Recruitment Channels lever defines how potential study participants are identified, reached, and onboarded to the Bonn residential unit. It governs outreach messaging, referral networks, and screening workflows that translate public interest into enrolled participants who meet the study's inclusion and exclusion criteria. Objectives include achieving the target enrollment (50–70 NREM parasomnia participants plus matched controls), preserving geographic and clinical diversity, and maintaining steady recruitment throughput to support Aim 2 phenotyping and the development of the event-triage tools. Key success metrics include enrollment pace, screen-to-enroll conversion, retention through the stay, and diversity indicators by age, sex, and disorder subtype.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Expanding recruitment channels accelerates enrollment and increases pool diversity, enabling more rapid data collection for longitudinal phenotyping. It creates strong synergy with the Data Acquisition Pipeline by supplying more eligible participants to instrument, and with Control Group Stratification by supporting balanced representation across subgroups.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include greater screening burden and potential sampling bias from broad channels, risking reduced generalizability. It also pressures Overnight Staffing Model and Data Sharing Scope, potentially increasing costs and complicating privacy controls across a more diverse participant pool.

characterized_levers.name: Overnight Staffing Model
characterized_levers.consequences: The overnight staffing model directly impacts participant safety, event capture rates, and technician workload. Increasing staff improves response time to events and annotation throughput, but raises personnel costs. Reducing staff may compromise safety and data quality, particularly if multiple events occur simultaneously.
options: Implement a hybrid staffing model where a single technician remotely monitors multiple suites via video and sensor data, with a second technician on-call for immediate in-person response to flagged events.
Cross-train research staff from the Department of Epileptology to provide supplemental overnight coverage during peak periods, leveraging existing expertise and reducing the need for dedicated hires.
Introduce a tiered response protocol where automated alerts trigger graduated levels of intervention, from remote observation to in-person assessment, optimizing technician time allocation.
characterized_levers.review: Adjusting staffing balances cost and responsiveness, but the options overlook the potential for burnout and attrition associated with demanding overnight shifts.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The overnight staffing model directly impacts participant safety, data quality, and the ability to respond to events, making it a core strategic decision.
characterized_levers.description: Purpose: The Overnight Staffing Model defines how night-time coverage is allocated across eight active suites, balancing safety, data capture, and technician workload. It defines shift patterns, on-call escalation, and response protocols during evenings and nights. Objectives include ensuring rapid event verification, minimizing false alarms, maintaining acceptable staff-to-participant ratios, and preserving staff wellbeing. Key success metrics include average response time to flagged events, missed events per night, overtime burden, and sustained annotation throughput without compromising safety.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Overnight staffing improves safety, reduces missed events, and increases annotation throughput. It synergizes with Nocturnal Safety Protocol by ensuring swift in-person checks when alerts trigger, and with Event Adjudication Protocol by enabling rapid follow-up assessment of flagged episodes.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include higher personnel costs and potential burnout; this can constrain Data Sharing Scope by limiting data-sharing commitments and Publication Target Breadth by straining dissemination resources, potentially impacting timelines.

characterized_levers.name: Data Acquisition Pipeline
characterized_levers.consequences: The data acquisition pipeline determines the richness and fidelity of captured data, influencing the accuracy of event characterization and the performance of event-triage tools. Increasing sensor density and sampling rates improves data resolution, but also increases storage requirements, annotation burden, and computational complexity. Reducing data volume eases processing demands but may sacrifice critical information.
options: Implement adaptive sampling rates that dynamically adjust data acquisition based on real-time event detection, increasing resolution during suspected parasomnia episodes and reducing it during periods of quiescence.
Prioritize specific sensor modalities based on their predictive power for parasomnia events, reducing the reliance on less informative channels and streamlining the data stream.
Integrate automated artifact detection and removal algorithms into the data pipeline, minimizing the need for manual cleaning and improving the efficiency of subsequent analysis.
characterized_levers.review: Modifying the data pipeline trades off data richness against processing efficiency, but the options do not address the potential for introducing systematic biases through automated pre-processing steps.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The data acquisition pipeline determines the quality and type of data collected, which is fundamental to achieving the research aims.
characterized_levers.description: Purpose: Data Acquisition Pipeline defines the end-to-end flow of sensor data—from dry-electrode EEG headbands and mattress sensors to video and ambient inputs—covering collection, synchronization, storage on NAS, and encrypted backups. It controls sensor density, sampling rates, and data routing into EEG-BIDS format. Objectives include maximizing data richness for parasomnia characterization while avoiding data loss and unmanageable storage or processing demands. Key metrics include data completeness per participant, time-synchronization accuracy, storage utilization, and latency in data availability for annotation and adjudication.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Higher data fidelity from a richer pipeline supports more accurate detection and adjudication. It synergizes with Event Adjudication Protocol by providing higher-quality segments for review and with Data Acquisition Triggering by enabling more reliable triggers and responsive escalation.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include higher storage and processing demands and potential bias from automated pre-processing. It can burden Data Sharing Scope due to privacy requirements and may necessitate tighter Environmental Cue Management to stay compliant, potentially slowing cross-site collaboration.

characterized_levers.name: Event Adjudication Protocol
characterized_levers.consequences: The event adjudication protocol directly affects the reliability and validity of the identified parasomnia events. More rigorous adjudication, such as requiring consensus from multiple expert raters, improves accuracy but increases scoring costs and turnaround time. Less stringent adjudication reduces costs but may compromise data quality.
options: Employ a machine-learning model pre-trained on a large dataset of polysomnography recordings to pre-screen potential events, reducing the number of segments requiring manual review by expert raters.
Implement a 'disagreement resolution' pathway where a third, senior expert adjudicates only those events on which the initial two raters disagree, focusing resources on the most ambiguous cases.
Establish a standardized training program for raters, incorporating regular calibration exercises and feedback sessions to minimize inter-rater variability and improve overall agreement.
characterized_levers.review: Adjusting adjudication stringency balances accuracy and cost, but the options fail to consider the potential for rater fatigue and the impact of subjective biases on event classification.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The event adjudication protocol directly impacts the reliability and validity of the identified parasomnia events, a core element of the research.
characterized_levers.description: Purpose: Event Adjudication Protocol codifies how nights and events are scored to identify parasomnia episodes. It sets scoring rules, reviewer roles, and turnaround expectations, including whether consensus is required or a third expert adjudicates disagreements. It documents blinding, data provenance, audit trails, and escalation pathways. Objectives include achieving reliable inter-rater agreement and timely event counts for Aim 2 analyses. Key metrics include inter-rater reliability, adjudication turnaround time, and the proportion of events adjudicated as parasomnia versus non-ephemeral artifact.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Reliable adjudication benefits from standardized annotation depth and higher-quality data. It synergizes with Annotation Review Depth and Data Acquisition Pipeline, reducing inter-rater variability and speeding review while preserving data provenance and auditability.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include higher adjudication costs and longer turnaround times, potentially conflicting with Data Sharing Scope restrictions and planned Publication Target Breadth if delays affect dissemination.

characterized_levers.name: Pharmaceutical Partnership Terms
characterized_levers.consequences: Securing a pharmaceutical industry partnership provides additional funding and potential access to proprietary compounds or technologies. However, it may also introduce conflicts of interest, restrict publication timelines, or influence the research agenda. Maintaining academic independence is crucial for preserving scientific integrity.
options: Negotiate a 'blinded' collaboration where the pharmaceutical partner provides funding and access to compounds, but remains unaware of participant-level data or specific research hypotheses until after publication.

Establish a clear 'firewall' between the academic research team and the pharmaceutical partner's marketing or product development divisions, ensuring that research findings are not used for promotional purposes.
Structure the partnership as a 'research consortium' involving multiple pharmaceutical companies, diversifying funding sources and reducing the influence of any single partner on the research agenda.
characterized_levers.review: Pharma partnerships offer funding but risk compromising research independence; the options neglect the potential for intellectual property disputes or restrictions on data sharing.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Pharmaceutical partnership terms are important for funding and collaboration, but the project's feasibility doesn't hinge on it, making it secondary.
characterized_levers.description: Purpose: Pharmaceutical Partnership Terms defines how potential industry support interacts with academic independence, data access, publication timelines, and IP ownership. It outlines funding mechanisms, governance boundaries, and safeguards to minimize influence on research questions or analyst decisions. Objectives include securing sustainable resources while preserving scientific integrity and participant protection. Key metrics include clarity of publication rights, number of negotiating milestones achieved, and independence safeguards enforced throughout the project lifecycle.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Pharma partnerships provide extra resources that can support broader publication and clearer data-sharing boundaries. It synergizes with Publication Target Breadth and Data Sharing Scope to align dissemination goals with partner expectations while maintaining governance and independence.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include potential constraints on publication cadence and data access policies, risking clashes with Event Adjudication Protocol processes and with Control Group Stratification when data-sharing or IP terms limit analyses.

characterized_levers.name: Residential Suite Configuration
characterized_levers.consequences: The configuration of the residential suites impacts participant comfort, safety, and data quality. More elaborate suites with advanced monitoring capabilities increase costs and complexity. Simpler suites reduce costs but may limit the range of observable behaviors and compromise participant comfort.
options: Designate a subset of suites as 'high-fidelity' rooms equipped with advanced sensor arrays and environmental controls, reserving them for participants with complex or high-risk parasomnia profiles.
Incorporate modular design elements into the suites, allowing for flexible reconfiguration based on individual participant needs and research protocols.
Prioritize participant comfort and domesticity by incorporating personalized lighting, soundscapes, and bedding options into each suite, fostering a more relaxed and naturalistic sleep environment.
characterized_levers.review: Suite configuration balances data capture and participant comfort, but the options overlook the potential for the suites themselves to influence sleep patterns and introduce artificiality.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Residential suite configuration impacts participant comfort and data quality, but is secondary to the overall safety and data acquisition strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The Residential Suite Configuration lever governs the physical and functional setup of the sleep units, balancing participant comfort, safety, and data capture capability. It dictates how many suites are designated high-fidelity with advanced sensors and environmental controls, how modular elements can be reconfigured by protocol, and how room features influence sleep behavior. Objectives include maximizing long-term data yield, enabling safe monitoring of complex parasomnia presentations, and maintaining participant well-being. Key success metrics: event capture rate, data completeness, incident frequency, participant satisfaction, and unit scalability within budget and staffing constraints.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: High-fidelity rooms enable richer sensor data and safer monitoring for complex cases, while modular design supports protocol-driven reconfiguration. It complements Nocturnal Safety Protocol by aligning safety features with observation needs and pairs with Suite Ambient Design to preserve comfort without sacrificing data richness.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: A highly-fidelity suites raise costs and staffing demands, potentially limiting overall scalability and data throughput. This lever's trade-offs with ambient design choices and with overall suite capacity, possibly increasing false alarms or altering sleep patterns if environments become too clinical. It may constrain budget for Data Acquisition Triggering and Nocturnal Safety Protocol adjustments.

characterized_levers.name: Suite Ambient Design
characterized_levers.consequences: The aesthetic and functional design of the residential suites directly impacts participant comfort and naturalistic behavior. A more clinical environment may increase participant anxiety and suppress parasomnia events, while an overly permissive environment could compromise safety. Balancing these factors is crucial for data quality and participant retention.
options: Prioritize a highly domestic aesthetic with soft lighting, familiar furniture, and personalized decor to encourage relaxation and natural sleep patterns
Implement a minimalist design with standardized layouts, neutral colors, and easily cleanable surfaces to facilitate efficient monitoring and minimize potential hazards
Offer participants a choice between several pre-designed suite themes, balancing domestic comfort with research requirements and allowing for some personalization
characterized_levers.review: A homelike suite design risks compromising data quality and safety, while a clinical design may inhibit natural behavior; the gap is a design that adapts to individual participant needs.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Suite ambient design is important for participant comfort and naturalistic behavior, but is secondary to the core safety and data acquisition strategies.
characterized_levers.description: The Suite Ambient Design lever shapes the sensory milieu of the residential rooms to influence sleep behavior, comfort, and safety during long-term monitoring. It governs lighting, sound, textures, and room layout in order to balance domestic comfort with research feasibility. Objectives include reducing participant stress, minimizing artifacts due to arousal or movement, and preserving ecological validity of nocturnal behavior. Key success metrics include participant retention, rate of environmental-related disturbances, data quality indicators, and ease of monitoring across suites. This lever interacts with Residential Suite Configuration and Nocturnal Safety Protocol to ensure safety while maintaining home-like ambiance.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: Aligns with Residential Suite Configuration to preserve domestic ambiance without compromising data richness, and with Nocturnal Safety Protocol to maintain safety while reducing environmental disturbances. It also supports Data Acquisition Triggering by creating stable sensor conditions that minimize artifacts.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: A highly domestic ambient design may conflict with clinical monitoring needs, potentially increasing artifacts or camera visibility, while preserving comfort. It can constrain budget for high-fidelity suites and limit flexibility for rapid reconfiguration. This may narrow choices for sensor arrays, influencing Data Acquisition Pipeline integration.

characterized_levers.name: Nocturnal Safety Protocol
characterized_levers.consequences: Safety protocols dictate the level of intervention during parasomnia events. Overly restrictive protocols may prevent the capture of complete events or introduce artificial awakenings, while insufficient protocols could expose participants to injury. The balance between safety and data integrity is paramount.
options: Implement a 'hands-off' approach, intervening only in cases of imminent danger as determined by pre-defined escalation criteria and real-time video monitoring
Establish a tiered intervention system, starting with verbal redirection and escalating to physical intervention only if necessary to prevent injury
Employ a proactive safety model with frequent room checks and sensor-triggered alerts to preemptively address potential hazards before escalation
characterized_levers.review: Strict safety protocols can disrupt natural sleep and parasomnia events, while lax protocols increase injury risk; the gap is a protocol that dynamically adjusts to individual risk profiles.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Nocturnal safety protocol is a primary concern, as it directly impacts participant well-being and the ethical conduct of the research.
characterized_levers.description: This Nocturnal Safety Protocol lever defines the sequence and intensity of interventions during parasomnia events to balance participant safety with data integrity. It specifies escalation criteria, permissible physical interventions, and observation standards, ensuring rapid, proportionate responses while preserving natural sleep patterns whenever possible. Objectives include preventing injuries, minimizing unnecessary awakenings, and enabling continuous recording. Key success metrics include injury rate, escalation frequency, participant distress, interventional latency, and adherence to consented procedures. Alignment with environment design and monitoring systems is critical to enable safe yet ecologically valid observation.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: Works with Residential Suite Configuration to ensure safety features are embedded without compromising comfort, and with Suite Ambient Design to create non-intrusive monitoring environments. It also supports Data Acquisition Triggering and Event Detection Automation by providing reliable, safe platforms for observation and rapid response.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: Stricter safety protocols can disrupt sleep continuity, increase participant stress, and limit ecological validity, potentially reducing observed parasomnia events. It may constrain the use of high-fidelity suites in early phases and complicate coordination with Event Detection Automation if device-triggered interventions require timing that conflicts with natural events.

characterized_levers.name: Data Acquisition Triggering
characterized_levers.consequences: The method for triggering enhanced data acquisition (full PSG) influences the richness and relevance of the captured data. Relying solely on scheduled nights may miss critical events, while continuous full PSG is resource-intensive and uncomfortable for participants. A hybrid approach is needed to optimize data yield.
options: Trigger enhanced PSG based on real-time technician observation of unusual behavior via video and audio monitoring, capturing events as they unfold
Schedule enhanced PSG nights based on participant-reported event frequency and timing, maximizing the likelihood of capturing typical episodes
Utilize machine-learning algorithms to detect potential parasomnia events from low-burden sensor data, triggering enhanced PSG automatically based on probability scores
characterized_levers.review: Technician-triggered PSG is subjective, participant-scheduled PSG relies on recall, and algorithm-triggered PSG depends on model accuracy; the gap is a multi-modal triggering system.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Data acquisition triggering determines when enhanced data is collected, directly impacting the ability to capture and characterize parasomnia events.
characterized_levers.description: This Data Acquisition Triggering lever defines when to upgrade from low-burden monitoring to enhanced PSG, balancing data yield against participant burden and resource use. It mediates the hybrid triggering framework across real-time technician observation, participant-reported events, and machine-learning predictions from low-burden sensors. Objectives include maximizing capture of clinically meaningful parasomnia events while minimizing unnecessary full-night recordings. Key success metrics include trigger accuracy (precision/recall), event capture rate, average number of enhanced nights per participant, and operational cost per data yield. It coordinates with the Data Acquisition Pipeline and Safety systems.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: Pairs with Data Acquisition Pipeline to ensure fluent data flow from sensors to enhanced nights, and with Event Detection Automation to trigger PSG when signals cross thresholds. It also aligns with Nocturnal Safety Protocol to ensure triggers occur within safe interventional boundaries.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: Heavier reliance on triggered PSG can strain scheduling and personnel, risking under-sampling if triggers err or are delayed. It may also pressure Data Acquisition Triggering to favor high-yield nights at the expense of participant comfort, and could conflict with Data Sharing Scope if data labeling lags behind.

characterized_levers.name: Event Detection Automation
characterized_levers.consequences: The level of automation in event detection impacts the efficiency of data processing and the accuracy of event identification. Fully automated systems may generate false positives or miss subtle events, while manual review is time-consuming and prone to human error. A balanced approach is essential.
options: Develop a rule-based system using pre-defined physiological and behavioral criteria to automatically flag potential parasomnia events for further review
Train a deep-learning model on a large dataset of annotated parasomnia events to automatically detect and classify episodes with high accuracy
Employ a hybrid approach combining rule-based flagging with machine-learning classification to leverage the strengths of both methods
characterized_levers.review: Rule-based systems lack nuance, deep-learning models require extensive training data, and hybrid approaches inherit the limitations of both; the gap is a system that adapts to data heterogeneity.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Event detection automation is important for data processing efficiency, but is secondary to the core data acquisition and adjudication strategies.
characterized_levers.description: This Event Detection Automation lever specifies the automation approach for detecting parasomnia events from recorded data, balancing rule-based flags, deep-learning classifications, and a hybrid approach. It aims to maximize true detections while minimizing false positives, enabling efficient prioritization for human adjudication. Objectives include reducing manual review time, improving consistency across scorers, and providing interpretable outputs for downstream analysis. Key success metrics include precision, recall, F1 score on event detection, inter-rater agreement improvements, and the proportion of events escalated to adjudication. It interacts with the Data Acquisition Triggering and Annotation Review Depth.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Synergy: Complements Data Acquisition Triggering by providing real-time event scores for triggers, and aligns with Annotation Review Depth to streamline adjudication with higher-quality evidence. It also supports Event Adjudication Protocol by delivering consistent, interpretable outputs for clinical review.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Conflict: Over-reliance on automation may reduce examiner oversight, risking missed nuance in ambiguous episodes and over-segmentation of events. It could conflict with Data Acquisition Triggering if algorithm confidence undercuts human decision-making, and with Annotation Review Depth if adjudication loads shift due to algorithmic misclassifications.

characterized_levers.name: Annotation Review Depth
characterized_levers.consequences: The intensity of manual review affects the reliability and validity of event scoring. Single-rater scoring is efficient but susceptible to bias, while multi-rater scoring is more robust but resource-intensive. The optimal balance depends on the study's specific aims and resources.
options: Implement a single-rater scoring system with periodic inter-rater reliability checks to ensure consistency and minimize bias
Employ a dual-rater scoring system with adjudication of disagreements by a senior sleep medicine physician to maximize accuracy
Utilize a tiered review process, with automated pre-screening followed by targeted manual review of ambiguous or high-priority events
characterized_levers.review: Single-rater scoring risks bias, dual-rater scoring is costly, and tiered review depends on pre-screening accuracy; the gap is a review process that adapts to event complexity.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Annotation review depth directly impacts the reliability and validity of event scoring, a core element of the research.
characterized_levers.description: Annotation Review Depth: This lever defines how event-scoring annotations are reviewed and consolidated across scoring tiers. It sets whether scoring is performed by a single rater, by two independent raters with adjudication, or via a tiered approach with automated pre-screening followed by targeted manual review. Its objectives are to maximize reliability and validity of parasomnia event labels while containing labor costs and review turnaround times. Key success metrics include inter-rater reliability (e.g., Cohen's kappa), adjudication resolution rate, per-event review time, and the proportion of events requiring downstream re-scoring, all aligned with Aim 3's evaluation framework.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Event Adjudication Protocol and Event Detection Automation. A tiered or dual-rater approach complements standardized adjudication workflows and automated pre-screening, reducing false positives and ensuring robust event labeling that feeds the semi-automated triage tools used in Aim 3.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include higher staffing costs when using dual or tiered reviews, potentially competing with Overnight Staffing Model constraints and budget realities. Prolonged adjudication cycles can slow data throughput and burden the Data Acquisition Pipeline, risking delays in timely event detection and timely scoring.

characterized_levers.name: Data Sharing Scope
characterized_levers.consequences: The extent of data sharing influences the impact and reproducibility of the research. Openly sharing all data maximizes transparency but raises privacy concerns, while restricting data sharing limits the potential for collaboration and validation. A carefully considered data-sharing policy is crucial.
options: Share only de-identified physiological data and summary statistics through a secure data repository with restricted access and data use agreements
Establish a collaborative data-sharing platform with select research partners, providing access to more detailed data under strict confidentiality agreements
Publish fully anonymized datasets with synthetic data augmentation to protect participant privacy while maximizing data utility
characterized_levers.review: Restricted data sharing limits collaboration, open sharing risks privacy breaches, and synthetic data may distort findings; the gap is a data-sharing model that balances access and privacy.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Data sharing scope is important for reproducibility and collaboration, but is secondary to the core research aims and participant privacy.
characterized_levers.description: Data Sharing Scope: This lever defines how raw, de-identified, and summarized data are shared with researchers, institutions, and repositories. It governs access controls, data use agreements, privacy safeguards, and retention timelines to balance reproducibility with participant protection and regulatory compliance. Choices include sharing only de-identified physiological data and summaries, establishing a confidential collaboration platform, or publishing fully anonymized datasets with synthetic augmentation. Success metrics include percentage of data released, time to access requests, breach incidents, and alignment with funder and institutional data policies.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Positive interactions with Data Acquisition Pipeline and Publication Target Breadth: clear sharing policies accelerate external replication and multi-site analyses, while detailed de-identified data under strict DUA accelerates grant proposals and peer review. Collaboration platforms enable external cohorts to benchmark Bonn results under agreed privacy constraints.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include privacy risk if scope is too broad, potential compliance delays if access controls are overly strict, and synthetic data possibly distorting findings. The gap is selecting a policy that preserves utility for validation while protecting participants, which can constrain open publication and cross-institution collaborations.

characterized_levers.name: Environmental Cue Management
characterized_levers.consequences: Carefully managing environmental cues can either promote or disrupt natural sleep patterns. Introducing specific light or sound stimuli could trigger or suppress parasomnia events, but may also alter sleep architecture and reduce the ecological validity of the data. A balance must be struck to maximize event capture without fundamentally changing the sleep environment.
options: Implement a fixed schedule of light and temperature changes to standardize the sleep environment and minimize external influences on sleep patterns
Introduce personalized pre-sleep routines based on participant habits to promote relaxation and natural sleep onset, while carefully documenting any deviations
Randomize exposure to subtle auditory or olfactory stimuli during sleep to probe for potential triggers of parasomnia events, while monitoring for habituation effects
characterized_levers.review: Standardizing environmental cues may reduce variability but also suppress naturalistic behaviors, and the options neglect the potential for participant-driven environmental adjustments.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Environmental cue management can influence sleep patterns, but is secondary to the core safety and data acquisition strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Environmental Cue Management: This lever governs the introduction, suppression, and timing of cues (light, sound, temperature, and odor) within the residential unit. It aims to balance ecological validity with data integrity by avoiding uncontrolled cues while enabling controlled probes when needed. It includes fixed schedules, participant-driven adjustments within safety limits, and occasional randomized cue exposures to probe trigger hypotheses. Success metrics: event capture rate and false-positive rate related to cues, participant comfort, protocol adherence, and consistency across nights.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Suite Ambient Design and Residential Suite Configuration. Coordinated ambient design ensures cues are delivered safely and unobtrusively, improving reliability of parasomnia capture while preserving a domestic environment.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include standardization that may reduce natural sleep variability, potentially biasing longitudinal phenotyping; over-manipulation could undermine Aim 2's ecological validity and participant comfort. Personalization needs must be balanced against safety and protocol fidelity, possibly constraining nightly scheduling if cues exceed comfort thresholds.

characterized_levers.name: Technician Training Focus
characterized_levers.consequences: The training focus for overnight technicians directly impacts both participant safety and data quality. Prioritizing safety protocols minimizes risk but may reduce time spent on detailed annotation. Conversely, emphasizing annotation accuracy could compromise vigilance in responding to participant events.
options: Prioritize comprehensive safety training, including de-escalation techniques and emergency response protocols, to ensure participant well-being above all else
Emphasize real-time annotation skills and AASM scoring criteria to maximize the accuracy and completeness of event logging during overnight shifts
Implement a blended training approach that balances safety protocols with basic annotation skills, supplemented by remote expert support for complex events
characterized_levers.review: Balancing safety and annotation skills requires a trade-off, and the options overlook the potential for specialized roles focusing on either safety or annotation.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Technician training focus directly impacts both participant safety and data quality, making it a core strategic decision.
characterized_levers.description: Technician Training Focus: This lever defines the priority emphasis for overnight technicians: safety and emergency responsiveness, annotation accuracy, or a blended approach. The chosen focus shapes real-time responses to events, accuracy of AASM scoring, fatigue management, and data throughput. Options include safety-first, annotation-first, or a blended program with remote expert support for complex events. Success metrics include incident response time, rate of near-miss events, AASM inter-rater reliability for nightly annotations, and staff retention.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Overnight Staffing Model and Annotation Review Depth, ensuring trained responders support high-quality logging and reliable adjudication workflows. A blended program also complements Event Adjudication Protocol by providing consistent documentation during complex events.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include potential stall in event recognition if safety dominates annotation training, or vice versa, reducing scoring completeness. It can constrain recruitment tempo or shift staff allocation away from data annotation tasks, conflicting with aims to achieve high-throughput event triage and long-term data quality; resources devoted to training may affect the Data Acquisition Pipeline.

characterized_levers.name: Event-Triage Confidence Threshold
characterized_levers.consequences: The confidence threshold for the semi-automated event-triage tool affects the balance between sensitivity and specificity. A low threshold increases sensitivity, capturing more true events but also generating more false positives that require manual review. A high threshold increases specificity, reducing false positives but potentially missing genuine parasomnia episodes.
options: Set a low confidence threshold to maximize sensitivity and capture all potential parasomnia events, accepting a higher rate of false positives requiring manual review
Establish a high confidence threshold to minimize false positives and reduce manual review burden, even if it means potentially missing some genuine parasomnia events
Implement an adaptive threshold that adjusts based on individual participant data and overall event frequency, optimizing the balance between sensitivity and specificity
characterized_levers.review: Adjusting the confidence threshold involves a sensitivity/specificity trade-off, and the options don't address the use of multiple thresholds for different event types.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: The event-triage confidence threshold affects the balance between sensitivity and specificity, but is secondary to the overall event detection and adjudication strategies.
characterized_levers.description: Event-Triage Confidence Threshold: This lever sets the threshold for the semi-automated event triage tool, balancing sensitivity and specificity. A low threshold captures more potential events but increases manual review load and false positives; a high threshold reduces false positives but risks missing genuine parasomnia episodes. An adaptive threshold can tailor to individual participants and overall event frequency, optimizing the trade-off across Aim 3. The objective is to maintain adequate detection while limiting reviewer burden and preserving data quality for Aim 3. Metrics: true-positive and false-positive rates, missed-event rate, and manual-review hours.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: Strong synergy with Event Detection Automation and Annotation Review Depth: adaptive thresholds complement automated detection and targeted manual review, reducing workload while preserving accuracy. It also informs the tiered review strategy used to adjudicate ambiguous events.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Trade-offs include potential bias if thresholds are poorly set, risking under- or over-reporting events and affecting generalizability. It can increase variability in reviewer workload across nights, challenging Overnight Staffing Model planning. Coordination with Data Acquisition Triggering may be needed to maintain pace.

characterized_levers.name: Control Group Stratification
characterized_levers.consequences: How the control group is stratified impacts the validity of comparisons and the generalizability of findings. Matching controls solely on age and sex may overlook other relevant factors influencing sleep patterns. More granular stratification improves the accuracy of benchmarking but increases recruitment complexity.
options: Recruit a control group matched only on age and sex to minimize recruitment burden and provide a basic comparison for nocturnal movement patterns
Stratify the control group based on age, sex, and sleep quality (e.g., PSQI score) to account for common sleep disturbances and improve benchmarking accuracy
Match controls individually to parasomnia participants based on a comprehensive set of demographic, lifestyle, and sleep-related variables to maximize comparability
characterized_levers.review: Control group stratification balances recruitment effort with benchmarking accuracy, and the options ignore the potential for using existing normative sleep data as a control.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Control group stratification impacts the validity of comparisons, but is secondary to the overall recruitment strategy and inclusion/exclusion criteria.
characterized_levers.description: Control Group Stratification defines how matched controls are selected and grouped for benchmarking against parasomnia participants. It determines whether controls are matched on age and sex alone or on additional factors such as sleep quality, comorbidity, lifestyle, and nocturnal movement, thereby shaping internal validity and generalizability. Objectives include reducing confounding, enabling meaningful contrasts of event yield, sensor accuracy, and annotation workload across groups, and facilitating subgroup analyses. Success metrics include recruitment success across stratified bands, balance on key covariates (PSQI, BMI, caffeine use), and stability of between-group effect estimates over time.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever strengthens benchmarking by enabling comparability between parasomnia and control groups. When aligned with the Data Acquisition Pipeline and Annotation Review Depth, stratification ensures that captured features and annotations reflect equivalent bases across cohorts, improving event-rate benchmarking, reducing bias, and supporting robust subgroup analyses.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: This constrains Recruitment Channels and complicates data harmonization across strata, risking underpowered subgroup analyses if strata become too granular. The team must balance precision with practicality to preserve study momentum.

characterized_levers.name: Publication Target Breadth
characterized_levers.consequences: The breadth of publication targets influences the dissemination of research findings and the project's overall impact. Focusing solely on high-impact sleep medicine journals may limit the reach to other relevant fields. Expanding the scope to include journals in related disciplines increases dissemination but may dilute the core message.
options: Target only high-impact sleep medicine journals to maximize visibility within the core field and establish credibility within the sleep research community
Expand publication targets to include journals in neurology, psychology, and engineering to reach a broader audience and foster interdisciplinary collaboration
Prioritize open-access journals and pre-print servers to ensure wider dissemination of findings, even if it means sacrificing some prestige associated with traditional journals
characterized_levers.review: Publication breadth trades focused impact for wider dissemination, and the options don't consider the strategic use of conference presentations to build momentum.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: Publication target breadth influences dissemination, but is secondary to the core research aims and the quality of the findings.
characterized_levers.description: Publication Target Breadth governs where and how findings are published, balancing core sleep-medicine journals with neurology, psychology, and engineering outlets. It shapes writing scope, methodological transparency, and the dissemination of secondary analyses, replication datasets, and methodological tools. Objectives include maximizing cross-disciplinary reach, attracting diverse funding, and accelerating translation to practice and policy. Key success metrics include the number of journals engaged, cross-disciplinary citations, uptake of open-data standards, and timely publication across venues, alongside evidence of reproducibility and external validation in multiple domains.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever synergizes with Data Sharing Scope and Environmental Cue Management by coordinating data-use standards and stable study conditions that support reproducible reporting. Publishing across neurology, psychology, and engineering audiences also increases cross-disciplinary collaboration, promoting external replication, methodological validation, and broader impact beyond sleep medicine.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Expanding publication targets can stretch resources, potentially diluting focus on high-impact sleep journals and delaying core findings. It may require accommodations with Data Sharing Scope and Pharmaceutical Partnership Terms, and, if a pharma partner is involved, align with their pre-publication rights and review windows.

characterized_levers.name: PSG Montage Density
characterized_levers.consequences: The density of the PSG montage during enhanced nights affects the richness of the physiological data and the burden on participants. A full high-density montage provides detailed information but can be uncomfortable and disruptive. A reduced montage is less burdensome but may miss subtle physiological markers.
options: Employ a full high-density PSG montage with numerous EEG channels, EOG, EMG, and ECG to capture the most detailed physiological data possible during enhanced nights
Utilize a reduced PSG montage with fewer EEG channels and only essential EOG and EMG leads to minimize participant discomfort and improve sleep quality
Implement an adaptive montage that adjusts based on individual participant characteristics and event frequency, optimizing the balance between data richness and participant comfort
characterized_levers.review: PSG montage density balances data richness with participant comfort, and the options overlook the potential for using wireless or dry-electrode sensors to improve comfort.
characterized_levers.deduplication_justification: PSG montage density directly affects the richness of the physiological data and the burden on participants, impacting data quality and participant comfort.
characterized_levers.description: PSG Montage Density governs the intensity of enhanced-night physiological recording. It decides whether to use a full high-density montage, a reduced set, or an adaptive approach, balancing data richness against participant comfort, sleep integrity, and operational workload. Objectives include maximizing event detectability for parasomnias while preserving tolerable burden and safety. Key metrics: proportion of nights with full vs reduced montage, data completeness, participant-reported comfort, and time to adjudication of events.
characterized_levers.synergy_text: This lever synergizes strongly with Data Acquisition Pipeline and Event Adjudication Protocol. A higher-density montage on targeted nights feeds richer raw signals into the pipeline and supports more reliable adjudication, while the reduced/adaptive mounts preserve comfort and enable efficient resource use. This balance also reduces fatigue and error rates among night staff.
characterized_levers.conflict_text: Higher montage density increases participant burden and demands more equipment, space, and staffing; it can strain Nocturnal Safety Protocols and Residential Suite Configuration. In exchange, it can constrain recruitment pace if controls must be matched on tolerance for instrumentation and limit flexibility in environmental cue management.
